DdnsProviderHintChangeIp: Username and Password are your ChangeIP account credentials.
DdnsProviderHintCloudNs: Update URL is the full ClouDNS Dynamic URL for the record. Keep it secret, since anyone with it can change the record.
DdnsProviderHintCloudflare: Set Auth email or token to the word token for a scoped API token, or to your account email for the Global API Key. Zone name is the zone, such as example.com.
DdnsProviderHintDdnsFm: Domain is your DDNS.fm domain. Key is the update key from your DDNS.fm dashboard.
DdnsProviderHintDdnss: Host is your DDNSS.de host. Key is your DDNSS.de update key.
DdnsProviderHintDigitalOcean: API token is a DigitalOcean API token with read and write scope. Apex domain is the domain, such as example.com.
DdnsProviderHintDinahosting: Username and Password are your Dinahosting credentials. Fill in Domain only when the host has more than two labels.
DdnsProviderHintDirectnic: Paste the full gateway URLs Directnic gives you for the record. Leave IPv6 gateway URL blank if you only update IPv4.
DdnsProviderHintDnsExit2: API key is your DNSExit API key. Domain is the domain, such as example.com, and the record name is used when it is left blank.
DdnsProviderHintDnsMadeEasy: Record ID is the numeric ID of the Dynamic DNS record. Record password is the password generated for that record.
DdnsProviderHintDomeneshop: API token and API secret come from the Domeneshop API admin.
DdnsProviderHintDonDominio: User is your DonDominio API user. API key is your DonDominio API key.
DdnsProviderHintDslReports1: Username and Password are your DSLReports credentials. This protocol carries IPv4 only.
DdnsProviderHintDuckDns: Labels are your Duck DNS subdomains, such as myhost. Token is shown at the top of duckdns.org after you sign in.
DdnsProviderHintDynDns1: Username and Password are your account credentials for the legacy DynDNS v1 protocol. This protocol carries IPv4 only.
DdnsProviderHintDynDns2: Username and Password are your account credentials. Server override defaults to members.dyndns.org and can point at a compatible service.
DdnsProviderHintDynadot: DDNS password is from the domain's Dynamic DNS settings at Dynadot. Domain is optional and splits the hostname into domain and subdomain.
DdnsProviderHintDynu: Username and Password are your Dynu credentials. Fill in Custom domain only for your own domain.
DdnsProviderHintEasyDns: Username and API token are your easyDNS API credentials.
DdnsProviderHintEnom: Base domain is your domain, such as example.com. Domain password is the domain's Dynamic DNS password.
DdnsProviderHintFreeDns: FreeDNS at afraid.org. Username and Password are your afraid.org credentials, used to get the update token.
DdnsProviderHintFreeMyIp: Domain is your freemyip domain. Token is from the link shown when you claim it.
DdnsProviderHintGandi: Set Auth keyword to the word token for a Personal Access Token, or any other value for an API key. Domain is the domain, such as example.com.
DdnsProviderHintGoDaddy: API key and API secret come from developer.godaddy.com/keys. Domain is the domain, such as example.com.
DdnsProviderHintHeNet: Record is the record name. DDNS key is the key dns.he.net generates for that record.
DdnsProviderHintHetzner: API token is a Hetzner DNS API token. DNS zone is the domain, such as example.com.
DdnsProviderHintHosting1984: API key is the FreeDNS API key in your 1984 Hosting account.
DdnsProviderHintInfomaniak: Username and Password are the dynamic DNS credentials you create in the Infomaniak Manager.
DdnsProviderHintInwx: Username and Password are your INWX DynDNS account. INWX works out the host from the account.
DdnsProviderHintIonos: API key is your IONOS API key, in the form prefix.secret.
DdnsProviderHintKeySystems: Password is the record's dynamic DNS password from the Key-Systems panel.
DdnsProviderHintMythicDyn: Username is your Mythic Beasts dynamic DNS API key. Password is its secret.
DdnsProviderHintNamecheap: Domain is your domain, such as example.com. DDNS password is from Advanced DNS after you turn on Dynamic DNS.
DdnsProviderHintNfsn: Member login is your NFSN member login and API key comes from Profile, then API. This protocol carries IPv4 only.
DdnsProviderHintNjalla: DDNS key is the dynamic DNS key Njalla shows for the record.
DdnsProviderHintNoIp: Username is your No-IP username or email. A DDNS key is safer than your account password.
DdnsProviderHintNs1: API key is your NS1 API key. Zone is optional and is taken from the record name when left blank.
DdnsProviderHintOvh: Username and Password are your OVH DynHost credentials. DynHost carries IPv4 only.
DdnsProviderHintPorkbun: API key starts with pk1_ and Secret API key starts with sk1_. Root domain is optional.
DdnsProviderHintRegfishDe: Update token is the regfish DDNS token for the record.
DdnsProviderHintSimplyCom: Account name is your Simply.com account number and API key is your Simply.com API key. Zone is optional.
DdnsProviderHintSitelutions: Record ID is the numeric ID from your Sitelutions Recordbook. Account email and Account password are your sign-in.
DdnsProviderHintSpaceship: API key and API secret come from the Spaceship API Manager. Domain is the domain, such as example.com.
DdnsProviderHintYandex: Yandex has retired the legacy PDD API, so updates are expected to fail. Move the domain to another provider.
DdnsProviderHintZoneEdit1: Username is your ZoneEdit username and DDNS token is your ZoneEdit dynamic DNS token. Zone is optional.

HelpMembers: Administrators may do everything, so no group holds them.

HelpProcessExpiredTask: Disables or deletes expired users and disables inactive users now.

HelpTroubleshooting: Holds the checks and repairs of each tool.
InactiveDaysHelp: The next Process expired and inactive users task run disables members with no activity for this long. Members who never signed in are left alone.
InviteGroupsHelp: Sets the groups a member's invites may join.
MaxInvitesHelp: Sets how many open invites a member may have. 0 is no limit.
MaxPeersHelp: Sets how many peers a member may have. 0 is no limit.
MovieQuotaHelp: Sets how many movies a member may request in the window Requests sets. 0 is no limit.
NewUserGroupHelp: Sets the group a new user joins. Everyone leaves them in no group.
PasswordChangesHelp: Sets whether members may set or change their own password. Administrators always can.
